children: are testing their 200-day moving average after a recent pullback, with momentum indicators weakening and the long-term trendline emerging as a key technical level.

The stock was around $942.64 on the daily chart, near the red 200-day moving average. The setup is similar to the March selloff, when Goldman Sachs found support around the longer-term trendline before reversing higher.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stood at 33.52, approaching the 30 level commonly associated with oversold conditions. Meanwhile, the MACD was below its signal line, with the histogram in negative territory.

The key technical question is whether Goldman Sachs can continue to hold the 200-day moving average and stabilize after the recent decline. A sustained hold could set the stage for a potential reversal, while a break below the trendline would put further attention on the stock's downside momentum.

title: Goldman Sachs tests 200-day average as momentum weakens
